newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria cabinet passes 1997 budget bill.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria cabinet passes 1997 budget bill.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet approved on Friday the 1997 budget bill assuming a lev/dollar rate of 500 and the implementation of a currency board, a government spokeswoman said.
She said the draft, which has yet to be debated and passed by parliament, assumed year-on-year inflation of 72 percent.
Bulgaria has agreed to introduce a currency board system proposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to boost confidence in the slumping lev and the crumbling financial system.
The lev has fallen from 70 to the dollar in January 1996 to 600 on Friday.
Under the system the amount of levs in circulation must be matched by the foreign exchange reserves and central bank lending to the government and commercial banks is severely curbed.
The system is expected to be introduced in February, after the terms of the programme are negotiated with an IMF mission, expected to arrive in January.

The government, which resigned two weeks ago, said that beside the draft 1997 budget, it will introduce to parliament in the next few days a package of legal amendments to make the currency board operational.
A new Socialist cabinet is expected to be formed by mid-month.
The draft envisages a budget deficit of 316 billion levs or 6.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Expenditure is assumed at 1.225 trillion levs and revenue at 909 billion levs.
GDP, which fell by 6.2 percent for the first half of this year, is seen falling a further 10 percent.
The socialist government had to revise its 1996 budget three times to accomodate rising domestic debt payments.
